Lessons.Title: Points, Lines, Rays, and Segments
ExplanationParagraphs:
Learning goal: You will identify and draw lines, segments, and rays.
In the previous lesson, you created drawings and used informal language to describe your drawings. You began to see segments as pieces contained within lines. In this lesson, you begin to connect points, lines, and line segments with formal definitions.

2021 lesson activities: Warm-up: Number Talk: Finding Differences (10 minutes); Activity 1: Card Sort: Who Am I? (20 minutes); Activity 2: Make Some Shapes (15 minutes); Cool-down: True or False: What’s the Point? (5 minutes)
Corrected mathematical focus: A line extends both ways, a ray has one endpoint and extends one way, and a segment joins two endpoints.

Edulytics authored guidance: Sort original figure cards by point, line, ray, or segment using endpoint/arrow attributes. On the point grid draw two connecting segments to create the requested figure. Explain how the same endpoints can define a segment, but a ray needs a specified starting point.
First-party Cool-down (not publisher assessment): Draw and label a ray starting at P through Q, and segment PQ.
Images, drawing/protractor accuracy, partner tasks and the gated original publisher Cool-down require original task evidence and teacher/visual review.
